evidence: Single executable entry point (Misery/__main__.py) with Pyrogram Client and idle() — typical of monolithic Python apps
Clear logical separation into modules/packages (cache, Downloaders, helpers, Misery, plugins) with minimal interdependencies (avg_fan_out=2.1)
Directory depth limited to 2, indicating flat, cohesive module structure rather than deep layered hierarchies
Shared dependencies across modules (e.g., helpers/admins.py imports cache.admins), but no explicit layer boundaries (e.g., no strict separation of persistence/service/controller)
Presence of domain-specific modules (Misery/song.py, Misery/VideoStreaming.py) handling core business logic alongside infrastructure concerns (Downloaders, helpers)
Config and helpers used as shared utilities — common in modular monoliths where modules share common concerns
Factors C1, C2, A3 (likely cohesion, coupling, abstraction) and T4, A1 (testability, abstraction) from metrics align with well-structured modular monolith
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., helpers/admins.py ↔ cache/admins.py) may hinder future modularity or testing
Mixing of infrastructure (Pyrogram, yt-dlp, ffmpeg) and domain logic in same modules (e.g., Misery/song.py) reduces testability and separation of concerns
No explicit boundary or port/adapter pattern to isolate external dependencies (Telegram API, YouTube services), increasing brittleness to changes
